value.body: Works out how much material, labour and money a construction project will take, starting from drawings and specifications. Employers include construction contractors, real-estate developers and quantity-surveying or project-management consultancies. A typical day involves taking quantities off drawings, preparing bills of quantities (BOQ), checking rates and helping price tenders.

items.label: Typical entry
items.note: A civil engineering diploma also leads to junior estimation and billing roles

items.label: Key references
items.value: IS 1200 (method of measurement), CPWD Schedule of Rates

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Many start as junior estimation or billing engineers at a contractor, or as site engineers who later move into estimation. Comfort with Excel, reading drawings and rate analysis is what interviews test. Short courses in quantity surveying are an optional add-on.

value.title: At a glance
items: Closely linked to quantity surveying, billing and contracts roles; titles vary by company.
Typical next roles: senior estimator, QS or contracts manager, cost manager.
Workload peaks around tender deadlines, so hours can be uneven.
